problem: Prior open-vocabulary object navigation only brings the robot near the target and ignores the robot's final orientation relative to the object (e.g. the front of a fridge or chair), which is required for follow-up manipulation. VLMs lack the 3D spatial understanding to output poses or trajectories directly.
motivation: Humans stand in front of a fridge to open it, not beside it. A navigation-to-manipulation gap arises if the robot ends at the side or back of the object. Visual prompting (marked images with numbered candidates) lets a VLM's common sense score candidate poses without a 3D semantic map.
key_idea: Use GPT-4V as a coarse-to-fine scorer: first pick the image where the target is visible, then score numbered circular candidate standing regions projected onto the image, and navigate to the best one and face the object.
insight: VLM outputs work better as heuristic scores over geometrically generated, visually-marked candidates than as direct plans. Ablations on HM3D (SR/SPL/DTG): full 0.43/0.26/0.56; directly navigating to the target 0.02/0.01/1.24; no task-aware space reconstruction 0.15/0.11/1.22; one-step instead of two-step goal decision 0.32/0.24/0.85. Local reconstruction and candidate scoring matter most, and the two-step re-decision gives a further gain.
method: Identification of Target Scene: GPT-4V with chain-of-thought is given the image set S (each image labeled with a red number) and the query, picks the clearest image containing the target, and the robot navigates to that image's camera position on a 2D occupancy map.

Reconstruction of Task-aware Space: SoM-style segmentation (SEEM/SAM) marks the image, the original and marked images are both fed to the VLM to get the target's mark ID, and the ID plus depth gives the target point cloud. The robot then rotates ±30° at two tilts (0° and 60° down) to build a point cloud around the target.

Generation of Location Candidates: RANSAC extracts the ground. Object, obstacle and ground points are projected onto a 1 cm 2D grid. Circular candidate regions of robot radius 0.2 m are sampled at 0.5–1.5 r_r from the object, pushed away from obstacles and de-overlapped (octree used for distance queries).

Sequential Decisions for Gazing: candidate circles are projected onto the image with numeric markers and GPT-4V scores them to choose one. The robot moves to the midpoint of the path to that circle, candidates are re-projected on the new view, GPT-4V makes a second selection, and the robot goes there and rotates to face the target.
Planning: the VLM only supplies subgoal scores. Motion is done by a standard 2D path planner on the occupancy map, and no 3D semantic map is built.

setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D with camera poses, an image set covering the scene and a 2D occupancy map
setting.action_space: low-level: stop, move_forward 0.1 m, turn_left/right 1°, look_up/down, with a 2D path planner over the occupancy map
setting.simulator: Habitat with HM3D v0.2 (plus a real-world custom mobile manipulator)
setting.privileged: pre-collected RGB-D frames with camera poses covering the scene, and a 2D occupancy map (a pre-exploration assumption)

numbers.eval_set_note: 9 HM3D scenes, 68 tasks in total. Table 1 covers Scenes A-F, random start poses; the split is not stated in the paper
numbers.extra: Uses pre-collected RGB-D frames and a 2D occupancy map. SR and DTG are redefined with orientation (success if DTG < 0.5 m to the optimal operation pose). Per-scene results, no aggregate.
numbers.evidence: Table 1 'Performance Comparison with all baseline', Navi2Gaze row

numbers.eval_set_note: Scenes G, H, I with initial poses at the side/back of the objects
numbers.extra: Start poses at the object's side or back. Orientation-aware SR/DTG. Compared against VLMaps only.
numbers.evidence: Table 2 'Comparing Performance of VLMaps with Initial Poses on Object Sides'

numbers_note: Results are per-scene fractions with no aggregate table. The paper text reports averages of a 61.9% SR increase and 68.8% DTG reduction relative to VLMaps. Real-world results appear only as a figure. The ablation (SR 0.43, SPL 0.26, DTG 0.56) equals the Scene I row and is run on HM3D.
results: Navi2Gaze beats SemExp, L3MVN and VLMaps on most scenes in orientation-aware SR and DTG, e.g. Scene C SR 0.95 / DTG 0.19 vs VLMaps 0.36 / 1.81. The paper reports an average 61.9% SR gain and 68.8% DTG reduction relative to VLMaps. VLMaps wins SR in Scene B and Scene F and SPL in Scene G. Real-robot demos on a fridge, water dispenser, drawer, chair and vending machine show better alignment than VLMaps.
limitations: Relies on an accurate segmentation and point cloud. Segmentation is sensitive to lighting and RGB-D depth is noisy.
Assumes a pre-collected image set and 2D occupancy map covering the scene (no autonomous exploration), and uses a closed GPT-4V.
Small custom evaluation (9 HM3D scenes, 68 tasks), only three weak baselines, and a redefined SR/DTG that is not standard.
